6.  Staff Reports
  ae  Director' s Report on Annual Discussion of Commission Bridget
  Priorities  Report and Presentation

  Mr. Wasserman reviewed the fiscal year 2025- 2026 budget priorities
  presentation and staff report. He recapped on last years budget priorities
  along with their progress and completions.

  Mr. Wasserman explained the City' s overall budget standings and future
  direction for the department that includes adjusting programming to assist
  with future savings.

  Mr. Wasserman introduced the City staff facilities and landscape division' s
  proposed projects that consist of City Hall, Community, Senior Center and
  Recreation center maintenances along with City Parks fences
  replacements throughout parameters.

  Commissioners provided the following list of priorities:
  Fire Alarm panels
  Park Restrooms improvements
  Pickleball courts
  Dog water fountain installation
  Fencing at City parks
  Installation of security cameras in City Parks
  Community Special Events maintain high quality and integrity of
  programming
  Youth recreation classes and programming that includes swim lessons
  Recreation Center, aquatic classes and Recreation center
  programming
  Motion:
  Commissioner Ash made a motion to approve and for staff to present the list of
  budget priorities discussed to City Council for consideration for FY2025- 2026,
  seconded by Commissioner Rodriguez and approved unanimously with the

  Chair Bartolo stated if the Urban Forestry Fund can be reconsidered.

  Commissioner Moon stated his excitement on the projects progressing, especialr7

  Commissioner Rodriguez requested for staff to notify the board whenever City
  Council discusses the Recreation Center and pools.

  01.

  Community member, Randall Howard, expressed his great interest in the bicycle
  master plan as he is a long- time rider himself and shared his point of view of the
  difference in bike lanes he currently encounters on his travels and stated that City of
  La Verne bike lanes are very accommodating and easy to see with the green and
  white street markings.

  Community member, John Ebiner, stated his concern that the bicycle master plan
  needs to coincide with the downtown specific plan upgrades as well to allow the
  growth of businesses and not to impede the parking situation on Bonita Avenue, W
  Ebiner ex pressed his support for the future that the bicycle master plan includes
  Arrow Highway,
